# Draft:H dwarf

----
An object with a spectral type H (also called H dwarf or hydrocarbon brown dwarf) is either a brown dwarf or a free-floating planetary mass object. They have a extremely low-mass for brown dwarfs (under the deuterium burning limit), and are predicted to be colder than Y dwarfs.
Characteristics
The spectral type H was first suggested in June 2025 by astronomers, Kevin Luhman and Catarina Alves de Oliveira after they discovered two unusual brown dwarfs. They are characterized by a presence of unknown aliphatic hydrocarbon in their atmospheres, and an absorption line at 3.4-3.5 μm.
H-type dwarfs have very low masses for brown dwarfs with a mass between 2 and 10 . The least massive H-type dwarf is approximately the same mass as Jupiter, making them the least massive brown dwarf spectral type. However, the least massive L-type dwarfs such as 2M1207 b have similar properties to H-type dwarfs.
Only two candidate H-type dwarfs have been found which are designated LRL 11001, and LRL 11003. There absorption lines are similar to the diffuse interstellar medium (also known as the ISM). Although, these two brown dwarfs may be H-type dwarfs they also have a similar spectra and properties to L-type dwarfs.
Location
Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Luhman and Alves de Oliveira were able to identify two potential H-type dwarfs in the IC 348 star-forming region. No other H-type dwarfs have been discovered in other regions, but there are predicted to exist in NGC 2024 (also referred to as the Flame Nebula), and  the TW Hydrae association.
